items.title: Donn Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 6, 2009
items.q: So Ronnie couldn’t go to Europe so we took Jimmy. And Jimmy also played with us in Carnegie Hall.

ctx.x: So who was your drummer mostly during those years?

Skooky Sherman was the first one, and then he graduated, and then for the times after that we were fortunate to be able to use two drummers from Utica. One of them, I think the first kid was Ronnie Zito who went on, he’s now a studio musician and worked with Woody Herman, a wonderful, wonderful drummer. And we couldn’t get him for a gig, and he says, “Well I’ve got this other fella, his name is Jimmy Wormworth, and he’d be more than happy to do it.” So we started alternating, you know, using them both. And then…

items.title: Jimmy Wormworth interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002
items.q: And Donn Andre is asking me if I’d be in Utica around that time.

ctx.x: And Donn Andre is asking me if I’d be in Utica around that time. The first week of June.
Yeah they rip it up. Yes indeed. Reunion Weekend.
